request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 5 beats run 1 in all 5 folds, but by small margins (0.001 to 0.025), so the gain is modest and the real difference is small.
Fold SD is about 0.07, so fold-to-fold variation is far larger than the gaps between the top configs. Run 5 and run 1 differ by only 0.009 in mean.
Run 5 also has the smaller model (num_leaves 8, min_child_samples 40), which fits the simpler-model preference.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin and may reflect past audit decisions rather than confirmed fraud. PR-AUC may therefore partly measure how well the model reproduces that labelling process.

ROC-AUC of about 0.944 is high and every config is close to it, which suggests strong signal in aggregate features. A possible leak or size proxy cannot be ruled out. Dropping size features lowers PR-AUC by about 0.03, so volume and size features carry some of the signal and may reflect scale rather than fraud.
Fold 3 is weak for every config (about 0.61 to 0.63), which points to a hard or distribution-shifted subset. Whether the folds are time-based or provider-grouped is not documented.
Precision@50 of 0.80 does not map directly to a queue of about 100. Precision at 100 was not reported and could be lower.
Runs 2 and 3 had no fold detail checked for run 2. Run 2 is clearly weaker on mean, so this is minor.
Only 5 configs were tried and the search was narrow. Further tuning would likely give gains within noise, so the decision is not sensitive to more search.
